rows.body: Illustrative brand-level patterns only—not a quote, financial model, or substitute for the franchise disclosure document, LOI, or your advisors. Use this tab to know what to ask and model, not what to sign.

Fee basis for royalty, marketing, technology, loyalty, and distribution (not the rate—the base)
Full initial term, renewal options, and notice obligations
PIP triggers at opening, conversion, and renewal
Performance test, cure period, and who can terminate after failure
Transfer, sale, and change-of-control approvals
Incentive package actually offered for this asset
Opening milestone schedule and who funds each phase
Mandatory systems and reporting beyond the fee line items

Owner typically funds: Front-loaded standards and FF&E alignment, technology cutover, working capital through opening, and application or training cash outlays.

Brand typically provides: Design and standards review, opening playbooks, pre-opening support, and milestone QA—not day-to-day operating spend.

Owner typically funds: Ramp marketing and loyalty enrollment while occupancy and rate build; recurring fees scale up as revenue mix stabilizes.

Brand typically provides: Negotiated ramp relief or co-op when offered, plus channel and mix guidance as the asset proves out.

Owner typically funds: The full recurring fee stack—royalty, marketing, technology, loyalty, and distribution—plus mandatory program participation once stabilized.

Brand typically provides: Sales and revenue support, brand systems access, and portfolio benchmarks—not property payroll or routine FF&E.

Owner typically funds: Renewal or conversion PIP, owner reserves, and re-licensing work when triggers hit—not part of steady-state operations.

Brand typically provides: Clear renewal standards; co-investment or phased PIP timing may be negotiable in competitive renewals.

rows.title: Application & Feasibility
rows.body: Align on asset fit, market, and conversion scope with brand development.

rows.title: Design & standards
rows.body: Kit-of-parts review, PIP scope, and approval milestones before major spend.

rows.title: Pre-Opening Planning
rows.body: Staffing, OS&E, systems implementation, and franchise readiness checklist.

rows.title: Opening Support
rows.body: Training, QA readiness, soft opening coordination, and brand-led launch touchpoints.

rows.title: Stabilization
rows.body: Heightened reporting and brand QA during early operating months; operator-led day-to-day where applicable.

Typical conversion path: feasibility alignment, design and standards approval, pre-opening execution with systems cutover, then stabilization with brand QA. Third-party operators often run opening while the brand approves milestones.

Financial planning themes (no deal-specific amounts on this page):

Front-loaded spend for standards compliance, FF&E, and technology cutover

Working capital held through ramp while mix and rate build

Fee stack that may step from opening/training-weighted to stabilized recurring charges

Potential incentive credits or ramps that change early-year cash burden

Reserve and PIP expectations documented for renewal—even if opening PIP is lighter

Model should separate owner-funded capex, brand/program fees, and operator pass-throughs

rows.title: To Join
rows.body: Application and entry fees; training and opening support; initial / franchise license fee; technology implementation / setup; plan review, design, or inspection fees. Basis and timing vary by keys, market, and deal—confirm in the FDD and LOI.

rows.title: To Operate
rows.body: Royalty, marketing fund, technology, loyalty participation, and reservation/distribution-related charges. Owners evaluate net contribution after mandatory program costs.

rows.title: When Things Change
rows.body: Renewal PIP, conversion PIP, termination-related obligations, and owner-funded reserves. Triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit—not steady-state operations.
Room count, market tier, new build versus conversion, incentive package, and whether a third-party operator leads opening usually change how fees and capital line items land on your deal.

rows.title: Term & renewal
rows.body: Expect a long initial franchise term with renewal options subject to notice, conditions, and brand standards compliance. Renewal may trigger property improvement expectations.

rows.title: Performance & exit
rows.body: Performance tests and QA programs are common—understand cure periods and who may terminate after failure. Early exit without cause may be limited; termination fees may apply depending on structure.

rows.title: Transfer & sale
rows.body: Assignment, change-of-control, and buyout provisions affect liquidity. Plan for brand approval paths before assuming a sale is frictionless.

rows.title: Area of protection
rows.body: Radius and restriction themes define how the brand limits same-brand competition near your site—confirm exact geography in legal documents.

Often negotiated in competitive markets. Brands in this tier may discuss key money, marketing support, fee ramps, or conversion assistance. Structure, timing, and clawback are deal-specific—confirm what was actually offered for your asset.
